findings.title: Blocked-email lookup can be bypassed by changing letter case or whitespace
findings.body: should_block? performs an exact database lookup with BlockedEmail.where(email: email), and neither BlockedEmail nor User normalizes email addresses before storage or comparison. PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, so registering with Bad@SpamExample.com or with surrounding whitespace bypasses a blocked entry stored as bad@spamexample.com. The blocklist therefore does not reliably block the addresses it is meant to block; both blocked entries and candidate addresses should be stripped and downcased consistently before comparison/storage.

findings.title: should_block? has a non-atomic write side effect during validation and can count one attempt multiple times
findings.body: should_block? increments match_count with a read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1; record.save) from inside email validation. Concurrent registration attempts can read the same count and lose increments, and ordinary flows that call valid? and then save (as UsersController#create does) run validation twice, so one signup attempt increments the counter twice and performs two writes. A predicate used by a validator should be side-effect-free, or the statistics update should be a single atomic increment performed once outside validation.

findings.title: Whitelist/blacklist domain regexp is not anchored to the end of the address
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})") with no end anchor or domain-boundary check, so it matches a substring anywhere after '@'. With a whitelist of gmail.com, an address such as user@gmail.com.evil.example passes because it contains '@gmail.com', even though its actual domain is gmail.com.evil.example; user@gmail.comm also passes. Domain restrictions should compare the parsed domain (including an end anchor) instead of searching for a substring.

findings.title: EmailValidator never checks that the value is a well-formed email address
findings.body: validate_each only applies the whitelist/blacklist settings and the BlockedEmail check; it adds no format error for malformed values. Since User now relies on validates :email, email: true for server-side email checking, a direct POST to UsersController#create (bypassing the client-side Discourse.Utilities.emailValid check) with an email such as 'not-an-email' passes validation whenever no domain whitelist/blacklist is configured, creating an account whose activation mail can never be delivered.

findings.title: rejectedEmails is a mutable array shared on the controller prototype
findings.body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined on the controller prototype, so the same array object is shared by every instance/reuse of the controller and is mutated by pushObject in createAccount. The list is never cleared, meaning an address rejected once (for example because it was temporarily blocked or taken) stays locally marked invalid for the rest of the session and can incorrectly block a later signup attempt with that address without any server re-check. It should be initialized per instance (e.g. in init) and reset when the modal/account flow starts.

findings.title: Specs stub out the integration they should prove, so a disconnected User validation would still pass
findings.body: The validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and invokes validate_each directly, while blocked_email_spec only tests BlockedEmail in isolation. No spec verifies that building/saving a User with a blocked email actually fails validation (i.e. that validates :email, email: true in User resolves to this validator, is loaded, and runs under the email_changed? condition), and there are no regression specs for the whitelist/blacklist behavior moved out of User. The whole feature could be unwired from registration and all new tests would still pass.
